Angular stylised 3D animation, brush-stroke texture, Essex coast, 1898, grey daylight from the east, black shadows.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:08. The shot opens on a medium shot low-angle view from the starboard rail out across a mile of open sea toward a hundred-foot Martian fighting-machine, a brass cowled hood on one long leg reaching forward and two long legs reaching back like a camera tripod, wading knee-deep far out in the water beyond the refugee ships; the paddle box fills the near right edge, the white rail crosses the lower frame, the fighting-machine rises out of the sea at the far centre, and the fleet of small steamers crosses the horizon. The camera is A low angle from knee height at the starboard rail looking up and out to sea at the fighting-machine a mile away, a 35mm lens, grey daylight comes from the RIGHT. At the first frame tHE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the fighting-machine far out in the sea; the paddle box fills the near RIGHT edge. The camera cranes up above the fighting-machine across the whole shot as the fighting-machine wades through the bright water, from 00:00 to 00:04. At 00:04 distant vessels turn across the sea, and the turn continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:08 the camera is craning up through the last frame, and the action continues with it, and the Martian towers beyond the rail, its tentacles enter the water, refugee vessels turn across the middle distance, and the coast lies behind them.
